name: Sayyid Ahmad Barelvi
role: Reformist leader of the Tariqah-i-Muhammadiya movement
contribution: Sayyid Ahmad Barelvi helped lead the Tariqah-i-Muhammadiya, an early nineteenth-century Muslim reform movement that combined Quran-and-Sunnah-centred religious renewal with organised opposition to colonial power and its regional allies. His preaching and network reached Bengal as well as North India.
context: Sayyid Ahmad visited Calcutta in 1820 and again in 1821, attracting a large following and preaching for several months. At this time Titu Mir became associated with his teaching; later Bengal activists and local networks connected religious reform with resistance to British authority. The movement's armed base shifted toward the north-west, where Sayyid Ahmad fought the Sikh forces of the region and was killed at Balakot in 1831.
impact: His legacy in Bengal lies less in direct command of a Bengali uprising than in the ideas, discipleship networks, and fund-raising links that helped shape later reformist resistance. In Bengal, the Tariqah-i-Muhammadiya influenced figures including Titu Mir and the Ali brothers, while the movement's later history also shows the tensions between religious reform, local custom, anti-colonial politics, and armed struggle.
highlight: Sayyid Ahmad Barelvi's reform movement connected North Indian religious renewal with Bengal networks of anti-colonial resistance.
seoTitle: Sayyid Ahmad Barelvi: Reform Leader and Bengal Connection
seoDescription: Learn about Sayyid Ahmad Barelvi, the Tariqah-i-Muhammadiya movement, his visits to Calcutta, Titu Mir's connection, and the 1831 Balakot campaign.
shortAnswer: Sayyid Ahmad Barelvi led the Tariqah-i-Muhammadiya movement, visited Calcutta in 1820–21, influenced Titu Mir, and was killed fighting Sikh forces at Balakot in 1831.

faq.question: What was Sayyid Ahmad Barelvi's connection to Bengal?
faq.answer: Sayyid Ahmad visited Calcutta in 1820 and 1821, where he preached the Tariqah-i-Muhammadiya and attracted followers. Titu Mir became associated with his teaching, and Bengal networks later helped support the wider movement.

faq.question: How did Sayyid Ahmad Barelvi die?
faq.answer: Sayyid Ahmad Barelvi was killed at Balakot in 1831 while leading the movement's north-western campaign against Sikh forces. His death did not immediately end the broader reform network, which continued in different forms.
